item.title: 【Introductions & Farewells】The Vault Is Open! | Meet LewsMediaVault
item.description:
Hey everyone!

I'm Lewis, better known as LewsMediaVault on here, and I'm from South Wales, UK!

I'm a huge music enthusiast, physical media collector and passionate advocate for media preservation, especially when it comes to music videos!

I've always had a fascination with the history of music videos, from original television broadcasts and rare masters to high-quality digital transfers.

I also enjoy working on my own restoration and remastering projects, experimenting with upscaling, deinterlacing, colour correction and other techniques to bring older recordings back to life while preserving their original character.

My music taste is all over the place (in the best way possible! XD), particularly 80s, 90s and 2000s music, including artists like Bananarama, Modern Talking and Britney Spears.

I created Lew's Media Vault out of my love for collecting, restoring and preserving media that deserves to be enjoyed for generations to come.

I'm here to discover rare gems, learn from fellow enthusiasts, contribute where I can and hopefully share some of my own projects along the way!

Looking forward to being part of the community!

Cheers, Lewis, LewsMediaVault!

item.description:
Fuzao (Chinese: 浮躁; pinyin: Fúzào; lit. "Restless") is the fourth Mandarin-language studio album (thirteenth overall) by Chinese singer Faye Wong. It was released on June 3, 1996, through Cinepoly. Wong took more artistic risks with her work as she approached the end of her record contract, resulting in the experimental nature of Fuzao. The album was positively received by critics, with The Straits Times considering the album as Wong's boldest and most artistically coherent effort to date. An alternative record, Fuzao was largely written and composed by Wong, with arrangement and production done by her husband, Dou Wei, and Zhang Yadong. The album features two collaborations (Tracks 4 & 8) with the Scottish dream pop band Cocteau Twins, whose sound and aesthetic were a heavy influence on Wong.
